newsitem.title: USA: Oregon House speaker seeks initiative reform.
newsitem.headline: Oregon House speaker seeks initiative reform.

text.p: Oregon House Speaker Lynn Lundquist introduced legislation on Friday to reform to the state's initiative process, a spokeswoman said.
Lundquist's proposal would create a committee that would review initiative measures, hold hearings and issue financial impact reports on the proposals.

The so-called Citizen Initiative Review Committee would consist of 12 members -- four appointed by the governor, four appointed by the president of the Senate and four appointed by the speaker of the House.
Lundquist said his proposal would not diminish the power of the initiative process. Reports issued by the committee would not be binding on the initiative sponsors.

"It (the legislation) simply aims to get objective information out to the public," Lundquist, a Republican, said earlier this week. "I believe the voters want to know if a ballot measure may be unconstitutional or if it has a fiscal impact that could affect their tax burden."
